title: Increase in Water and Electricity Rates / Align Rate Structure / Programs to Assist Reducing Water and Electricity Usage
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council REQUEST the Department of Water and Power (LADWP) to report back in 30 days with: Factors that have led to increases in water and electricity rates over the past ten years, since the 2016 rate increases, and a comparison of typical bills in the ten hottest neighborhoods in Los Angeles; Options for aligning rate structure to encourage optimal power usage, including timing and location of smart meter installation and shift toward time-of-use metering; Reasons why customers whose meters are accessible might receive bills with estimated rather than actual usage, or miss entire billing cycles; how LADWP ensures that in such circumstances actual usage is not billed in a higher rate tier; and how LADWP might proactively inform customers of payment programs; Feasibility of detecting anomalous water and/or electricity usage before the end of a billing cycle, and proactively informing customers, and/or allowing customers to receive frequent updates regarding actual utility usage; and Programs to assist customers in reducing water and electricity usage, including energy audits and energy-efficiency programs; and options for proactively providing information about these programs to lower-income households or communities, or customers with higher usage I FURTHER MOVE that LADWP include in this report a transparent breakdown of the effective residential rate per kilowatt-hour ($/kWh), specifically isolating how non-base formulaic pass-through adjustments—such as the Variable Energy Adjustment (VEA), Reliability Cost Adjustment (RCA), and Capped Renewable Energy Adjustment (CREA)—escalated total customer bills independent of base rates and actual household power consumption. I FURTHER MOVE that the Office of the Ratepayer Advocate be REQUESTED to review, check, and verify LADWP's data, methodology, and findings.
